questions.stem: A 30-year-old man presents to the ED for the third time in 2 years with flank pain and hematuria. CT shows a 4 mm calcified ureteral stone and incidentally notes multiple cystic dilations in the renal medulla bilaterally. Which condition best explains the incidental finding?
explanations: Incorrect. ADPKD produces cysts throughout the cortex and medulla and enlarged kidneys, not medulla-limited cystic dilations.
Correct. Medullary sponge kidney causes malformation of the terminal collecting ducts with small cystic dilations confined to the renal medulla and recurrent calcium stones.
Incorrect. Simple renal cysts are solitary and cortical, not clustered cystic dilations in the medulla.
Incorrect. Acquired cystic kidney disease occurs in patients with chronic kidney disease on long-term dialysis.
Incorrect. RCC produces a solid mass, not bilateral medullary cystic dilations.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old asymptomatic woman is found to have medullary sponge kidney on imaging done for an unrelated reason. Which anatomic structure is malformed in this disease?
explanations: Incorrect. The glomerulus is not the structure malformed in MSK.
Incorrect. The proximal tubule is in the cortex and is not affected.
Incorrect. The loop of Henle is not the site of the malformation.
Correct. MSK is characterized by malformation and cystic dilatation of the terminal (distal) collecting ducts within the renal medulla.
Incorrect. The renal pelvis is normal; the abnormality is in the medullary collecting ducts.

questions.stem: A medical student is reviewing the embryologic basis of medullary sponge kidney. Which developmental disruption is proposed to underlie the disease?
choices: Failure of pronephros regression in utero
Mesonephric duct agenesis with renal aplasia
explanations: Incorrect. Pronephros regression is not implicated in MSK.
Incorrect. Mesonephric duct agenesis would cause more severe renal malformations.
Correct. MSK is proposed to arise from a disruption at the interface between the ureteric bud and metanephric blastema during embryogenesis, leading to distal collecting duct dilatation.
Incorrect. Cloacal septation defects produce anorectal and urogenital anomalies, not MSK.
Incorrect. A persistent allantois forms a urachal anomaly, not MSK.

questions.stem: Researchers have proposed a candidate gene that may contribute to medullary sponge kidney, though no definitive cause has been established. Which gene has been studied?
explanations: Incorrect. PKD1 mutations cause autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
Incorrect. PKD2 is the second ADPKD gene, not implicated in MSK.
Correct. Mutations in the glial cell-derived neurotropic factor (GDNF) gene have been proposed as a possible cause of MSK, although no definitive genetic cause is established.
Incorrect. NPHP1 mutations cause nephronophthisis.
Incorrect. UMOD mutations cause autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man with medullary sponge kidney is being counseled about his condition. What is the most common clinical course of MSK?
explanations: Incorrect. Progression to renal failure is rare in MSK.
Incorrect. Dialysis is not the expected course; kidney function is usually preserved.
Correct. Most patients with MSK remain asymptomatic for life; symptomatic disease typically manifests as stones, UTIs, or hematuria.
Incorrect. Severe hypertension is not a defining feature of MSK.
Incorrect. MSK is a tubular/collecting duct disorder and does not cause nephrotic syndrome.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with known medullary sponge kidney presents with recurrent flank pain. Which symptom is the most common presentation in symptomatic MSK?
explanations: Incorrect. Edema is not a feature of MSK.
Incorrect. Proteinuria is not the presenting symptom.
Incorrect. Kidneys are typically normal in size in MSK.
Correct. Symptomatic MSK most commonly presents with symptoms of kidney stones, especially flank pain and hematuria.
Incorrect. Acute kidney injury is rare and not the typical presentation.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman with MSK develops recurrent urinary frequency and dysuria. Which complication does this finding suggest?
explanations: Incorrect. Nephrotic syndrome presents with edema and proteinuria, not dysuria.
Correct. Patients with MSK have an increased risk of urinary tract infections, presenting with urinary frequency and dysuria.
Incorrect. RCC typically presents with hematuria, flank pain, and a mass, not isolated dysuria.
Incorrect. Bladder cancer presents with painless hematuria, not dysuria as the dominant symptom.
Incorrect. Acute glomerulonephritis presents with hematuria, hypertension, and edema.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy with hemihypertrophy, macroglossia, and a history of omphalocele is found to have cystic dilations of the medullary collecting ducts on imaging. Which syndrome is most likely associated?
explanations: Correct. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (hemihypertrophy, macroglossia, omphalocele, gigantism) is among the conditions associated with MSK.
Incorrect. Tuberous sclerosis is associated with angiomyolipomas, not MSK.
Incorrect. VHL is associated with renal cell carcinoma and hemangioblastomas.
Incorrect. Alport syndrome causes hereditary nephritis and sensorineural deafness.
Incorrect. Turner syndrome is associated with horseshoe kidney, not MSK.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man with joint hyperlaxity, long extremities, and lens dislocation is incidentally found to have MSK. Which connective tissue disorder is most likely associated?
explanations: Incorrect. Ehlers-Danlos features hyperextensible skin and joint hypermobility but is not the brick's listed MSK association.
Correct. Marfan syndrome (joint laxity, aortic root dilation, lens dislocation) is among the conditions associated with MSK.
Incorrect. OI causes brittle bones, blue sclerae, and is not associated with MSK.
Incorrect. Loeys-Dietz causes aortic aneurysms and is not associated with MSK.
Incorrect. Pseudoxanthoma elasticum affects elastic fibers in skin, eyes, and vasculature, not MSK.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with MSK undergoes a CT scan with contrast. Which radiographic appearance is most characteristic of MSK?
choices: Bilateral enlarged kidneys with multiple cortical cysts
explanations: Incorrect. Bilateral enlarged kidneys with cortical cysts describe ADPKD.
Incorrect. A staghorn calculus suggests struvite stones from chronic infection.
Correct. CT with contrast or IVP shows a paintbrush (calyceal brush-like) appearance from contrast pooling in dilated medullary tubules in MSK.
Incorrect. Hydronephrosis with cortical thinning reflects chronic obstruction, not MSK.
Incorrect. Bilateral small echogenic kidneys reflect chronic kidney disease, not MSK.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman undergoes renal ultrasound for evaluation of recurrent stones. The study reports echogenic medullary pyramids. Which diagnosis is most consistent?
explanations: Incorrect. Pyelonephritis shows enlarged kidneys with hypoechoic areas, not echogenic pyramids.
Correct. Renal ultrasound in MSK can show echogenic medullary pyramids from the cystic dilations and interstitial calcifications, though findings may be subtle.
Incorrect. Renal artery stenosis shows asymmetric kidney size and is diagnosed with Doppler.
Incorrect. Diabetic nephropathy does not produce echogenic medullary pyramids.
Incorrect. Membranous nephropathy is a glomerular disease and has no characteristic ultrasound finding.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man with MSK has a histologic specimen examined after partial nephrectomy for unrelated reasons. Which histologic features are most characteristic?
choices: Cellular crescents within Bowman space of glomeruli
Dilated medullary ducts with interstitial calcium deposits
Diffuse tubular atrophy with cortical interstitial fibrosis
Sclerotic glomeruli with diffuse mesangial expansion
Caseating granulomas with multinucleated giant cells
explanations: Incorrect. Crescents indicate rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.
Correct. MSK histology shows cystic dilations of the medullary collecting ducts with interstitial calcifications appearing as black deposits on stain.
Incorrect. Cortical tubular atrophy is a nonspecific chronic injury pattern, not MSK.
Incorrect. Sclerotic glomeruli with mesangial expansion suggest diabetic nephropathy.
Incorrect. Caseating granulomas indicate tuberculosis or sarcoid involvement.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with MSK has serum bicarbonate of 18 mEq/L, urine pH of 6.5, and a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which complication does this represent?
explanations: Correct. MSK can be complicated by distal RTA from poor renal secretion of hydrogen ions, producing a non-anion-gap acidosis with inappropriately alkaline urine.
Incorrect. Type 2 RTA reflects proximal bicarbonate reabsorption failure and is not the brick's listed MSK complication.
Incorrect. Type 4 RTA is associated with hypoaldosteronism and hyperkalemia.
Incorrect. Lactic acidosis is an anion-gap acidosis from impaired tissue oxygenation.
Incorrect. DKA produces an anion-gap acidosis with ketones, not the picture described.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with MSK reports polyuria and polydipsia. Workup reveals dilute urine that does not concentrate after water deprivation or desmopressin. Which complication explains her findings?
explanations: Incorrect. Central DI responds to desmopressin because ADH deficiency is corrected.
Correct. MSK can cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus from decreased renal concentrating ability at the distal nephron, with no response to desmopressin.
Incorrect. Primary polydipsia responds to water restriction and is not caused by tubular dysfunction.
Incorrect. SIADH causes hyponatremia and concentrated urine, not polyuria.
Incorrect. Cerebral salt wasting causes hyponatremia with volume depletion, not the picture described.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman with longstanding MSK has a noncontrast CT scan showing diffuse parenchymal calcifications throughout both kidneys. Which complication does this represent?
explanations: Incorrect. Nephrolithiasis refers to discrete stones, not diffuse parenchymal calcification.
Incorrect. RCC is a solid mass, not diffuse calcification.
Correct. Nephrocalcinosis, or diffuse renal parenchymal calcification, is a recognized complication of MSK from abnormal distal tubular function.
Incorrect. ADPKD produces cysts, not diffuse calcification.
Incorrect. Renal infarction produces wedge-shaped perfusion defects, not diffuse calcification.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man with recurrent stones is diagnosed with MSK. He undergoes stone analysis. Which stone composition is most common in MSK?
explanations: Correct. Calcium stones are the most common type of renal stone in patients with MSK.
Incorrect. Cholesterol stones form in the gallbladder, not the kidney.
Incorrect. Cystine stones occur in cystinuria, not as the typical MSK stone.
Incorrect. Struvite stones form in chronic urease-producing UTIs, not as the primary MSK stone.
Incorrect. Uric acid stones occur in low urine pH or gout, not as the typical MSK stone.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman with MSK has had three calcium stones in the past year. She is counseled on prevention. Which recommendation is first-line?
choices: Bed rest and reduced physical activity in the home
High-calcium diet with vitamin D supplementation
Immediate surgical removal of asymptomatic small stones
Lifelong daily antibiotic prophylaxis with nitrofurantoin
explanations: Incorrect. Activity restriction does not prevent stone formation.
Incorrect. High calcium and vitamin D supplementation can worsen hypercalciuria-driven stone risk.
Incorrect. Small stones often pass spontaneously; immediate surgery is not first-line prevention.
Correct. First-line prevention of recurrent stones in MSK is increased fluid intake combined with dietary modifications.
Incorrect. Antibiotic prophylaxis treats infections but does not prevent calcium stone recurrence.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman with MSK and recurrent calcium stones has a 24-hour urine showing hypercalciuria. Which pharmacologic agent is recommended to reduce urinary calcium excretion?
explanations: Incorrect. Loop diuretics increase urinary calcium excretion and worsen stone risk.
Correct. Thiazide diuretics lower urinary calcium excretion and are used for stone prevention in MSK with hypercalciuria.
Incorrect. Acetazolamide alkalinizes the urine and can promote calcium phosphate stones.
Incorrect. Potassium-sparing diuretics have a minimal effect on urinary calcium and are not first-line for stone prevention.
Incorrect. Mannitol is an osmotic agent used acutely, not for chronic stone prevention.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man with MSK presents with fever, dysuria, and CVA tenderness. Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteriuria. Which is the appropriate next step in management?
explanations: Incorrect. UTIs in MSK require antimicrobial treatment, not observation.
Incorrect. Fluids alone are inadequate for an established UTI.
Correct. UTIs in MSK are treated with appropriate antimicrobial therapy, as in any patient with a UTI.
Incorrect. Nephrectomy is not indicated for UTI management.
Incorrect. Corticosteroids worsen infection and are not indicated.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man with MSK asks about his long-term outlook. Which best describes the prognosis of MSK?
choices: Most progress to end-stage renal disease
Most require kidney transplant by age 50
Rapid decline within 5 years of diagnosis
explanations: Incorrect. Progression to ESRD is rare and occurs only with recurrent obstruction or infection.
Incorrect. Transplant is not typically needed for MSK.
Correct. MSK has an excellent prognosis; renal function tends to remain normal unless there is recurrent obstruction or infection.
Incorrect. Rapid renal decline is not the typical course of MSK.
Incorrect. Nephrotic syndrome is not a feature of MSK.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old patient with MSK has a CT scan with contrast. Where are the cystic dilations and contrast pooling located?
explanations: Incorrect. The cortex is not involved in MSK.
Correct. The cystic dilations of MSK are confined to the renal medulla; the cortex is not involved.
Incorrect. MSK spares the cortex; involvement is medulla-limited.
Incorrect. The renal pelvis is not the site of MSK cystic dilations.
Incorrect. The ureter is not involved in MSK.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man with MSK is brought in by family because he had a febrile UTI 2 years ago and now has flank pain. Imaging shows obstructing stone with hydronephrosis. The disease is described as causing what?
choices: Acquired loss of functioning glomeruli over time
Autoimmune destruction of nephrons by antibodies
Ischemic vascular insult to the renal cortex
Tumor compression of the renal pelvis and ureter
explanations: Incorrect. MSK does not involve acquired glomerular loss.
Correct. MSK is a congenital condition characterized by malformation of the terminal collecting ducts in the medullary pyramids.
Incorrect. MSK is not autoimmune.
Incorrect. MSK is not vascular in origin.
Incorrect. MSK is not caused by tumor compression.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman is being worked up for medullary sponge kidney. Which lab pattern is consistent with MSK?
choices: Markedly elevated serum creatinine with oliguria
Massive proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and edema
Marked anion-gap metabolic acidosis with high lactate
explanations: Incorrect. Serum creatinine is typically normal in MSK; renal function is preserved.
Incorrect. Severe hyperkalemia is not a feature of MSK.
Correct. There are no specific lab findings, but patients may have hematuria, stone-disease urine crystals, and decreased serum bicarbonate from distal RTA.
Incorrect. Massive proteinuria suggests nephrotic syndrome, not MSK.
Incorrect. The acidosis of MSK is a non-anion-gap acidosis from distal RTA, not an anion-gap acidosis.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with MSK undergoes a CT IVU. The radiologist describes streaky contrast filling dilated tubules within the renal medulla. What is this finding called?
explanations: Incorrect. The doughnut sign is associated with other imaging contexts, not MSK.
Incorrect. Putty kidney refers to chronic tuberculous calcification.
Incorrect. Comma-shaped sign is not the MSK descriptor.
Correct. The paintbrush (calyceal brush-like) appearance describes streaky contrast filling dilated medullary tubules on IVP or CT-IVU and is characteristic of MSK.
Incorrect. Onion-skin appearance describes Ewing sarcoma periosteal reaction, not MSK.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man with MSK passes a small calcified ureteral stone after IV fluids and analgesia. He is counseled on long-term management. Which best summarizes MSK treatment?
choices: Curative surgical resection of all medullary cysts
Early dialysis access placement for ESRD
explanations: Incorrect. There is no curative surgical treatment for the cystic dilations of MSK.
Incorrect. MSK is not autoimmune; immunosuppression has no role.
Correct. The only treatment in MSK targets complications: stones, UTIs, and flank pain. The underlying malformation does not require treatment.
Incorrect. Most patients never progress to dialysis-requiring disease.
Incorrect. Corticosteroids have no role in MSK management.
